steps.title: Attack Lab tab on the LLM gateway demo page
steps.what: The Attack Lab is a tab on the LLM gateway demo page.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.

steps.title: Demo backend and scenario runners
steps.what: Tool Abuse is described as going through the demo backend, a token exchange, the Authorize resource-owner check and a balance read; it is a non-mutating simulation and not an AI Guard verdict.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.

steps.title: Hostile MCP demo server
steps.what: Tool Poisoning is described as going from hostile MCP tool metadata to a model proposal to the MCP tool-call boundary.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.

steps.title: MCP input-schema boundary
steps.what: Schema Violation is designed to send invalid arguments to the MCP input-schema boundary and to be labelled a local schema rejection unless the response reports a Privilege decision.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.

steps.title: Agent-to-agent specialist gate
steps.what: Inter-Agent Abuse is designed to send agent-to-agent discovery and message probes to the specialist agent's gate and show the HTTP response.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.

steps.title: Privilege LLM Gateway and model provider
steps.what: Malicious Content is designed to send a safe awareness sample through the Privilege LLM Gateway to the model provider, only on explicit action.
steps.why: A customer needs to see attacks run against the demo agent and to know which component stopped each one.
